text:
Mike C: Heads up — Polaris (enterprise) asking for a Dedicated commit in eu-west. Request: 40 A100-equivalent GPUs with 25% burst buffer, target start May 1. Sales wants a sizing + cost summary for tomorrow's call. They say current is ~10M tokens/day, projected 2.5x in Q3.

Tara L: Quick q — is 40 their asks or our initial recommendation?

Mike C: They proposed 40 as a starting point. They want us to validate. Also asked about auto-burst rules and fallback model mix for cost control.

Juniper: OK. Need to translate tokens -> GPU hours. Do we have their average seq length / tokens per request?

Mike C: Polaris gave sample: avg seq 220 tokens, avg 0.9 responses per session. Peak traffic window 10:00-18:00 CET, about 65% of daily load.

Priya S: Rough back-of-envelope: if baseline 40 GPUs at ~60% util and 24h, GPU-hours/day = 40 * 24 * 0.6 = 576. With 25% burst buffer that's another ~144 GPU-hours/day as headroom. But that ignores peak concentration.

Aidan: We should project peak-hour operating needs separately. If 65% of daily tokens happen in 8h, hourly demand during peak = (total_daily_gpu_hours * 0.65)/8. That can exceed baseline.

Juniper: Example calc in case it helps:
```
# rough GPU-hours calc
baseline_gpus = 40
avg_util = 0.6
gpu_hours_day = baseline_gpus * 24 * avg_util  # 576
burst_headroom = gpu_hours_day * 0.25                # 144
peak_window_hours = 8
peak_hourly_gpu_equiv = (gpu_hours_day * 0.65) / peak_window_hours
# if peak_hourly_gpu_equiv > baseline_gpus then burst needs to cover the delta
```

Tara L: Using that, peak_hourly_gpu_equiv = (576 * 0.65)/8 = ~46.8 GPUs equivalent during peak — so baseline 40 isn't enough for peak without burst or autoscale.

Priya S: Cost side: committed vs burst pricing matters. If customer wants firm SLA for p99 latency, we need reserved capacity priced higher. If we rely on burst, we expose them to throttling during noisy neighbor events unless we reserve cross-region fallbacks.

Mike C: Sales asked for two options in the deck: (A) conservative commit — 50 GPUs committed, 10% burst; (B) lean commit — 35 GPUs committed + 40% burst and fallback to smaller quantized model for non-latency-critical calls. Want cost delta and operational tradeoffs.

Aidan: Operational notes: burst above physical commit will consume our burst pool; if multiple customers burst simultaneously we may throttle or route to other regions (higher latency). We can implement model-fallback policies in the router to avoid hard capacity failures.

Juniper: For the deck, recommend we show: committed GPUs, effective peak capacity (committed + burst usable without cross-region), latency SLA risk, fallback plan, and approximate delta in monthly cost.

Priya S: I'll run pricing for both options — need committed unit price / GPU-hour + burst premium. Also include estimate for model quantization uplift (smaller model -> ~30-40% token cost reduction, but some quality risk).

Tara L: Also call out network egress considerations for eu-west start if they plan multi-region fallbacks. Cross-region fallback could increase latencies by 50-120ms and add egress costs.

Mike C: Action items:
- Priya: cost calc for Option A and B with monthly examples (due EOD).
- Aidan/Juniper: confirm router policies we can apply (model fallback, per-customer burst caps).
- Tara: prepare short slide on latency & egress tradeoffs.
- Mike: coordinate with Sales and draft proposal.

ops-bot: Reminder — dedicated commitment template (polaris-enterprise) created: https://redwood.internal/commits/PR-3812

Juniper: I'll validate numbers against historical eu-west traffic templates and flag any additional headroom we should demand.

Priya S: FYI — if they want strict p99 < 200ms for generation we should strongly recommend Option A or commit to model-fallback SLA.

Mike C: Thanks all — please drop short bullets into the shared doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/polaris-dedicated-proposal before 17:00 CET so Sales can finish the deck. :thumbsup:
